events.title: Execution of King Louis XVI
events.description: Louis XVI of France was guillotined in the Place de la Révolution in Paris after being convicted of treason by the National Convention during the French Revolution.
events.significance: His death ended the thousand-year tradition of French monarchy for the time being and marked a radical turning point in the Revolution, intensifying conflict between revolutionary France and the monarchies of Europe.

events.title: Death of Vladimir Lenin
events.description: Vladimir Lenin, founder of the Russian Communist Party and first head of the Soviet government, died at age 53 at his estate in Gorki after a series of strokes.
events.significance: His death triggered a power struggle within the Soviet leadership that ultimately led to Joseph Stalin's rise to supreme power and shaped the future course of the Soviet Union.

events.title: Death of George Orwell
events.description: English author Eric Arthur Blair, known as George Orwell, died of tuberculosis in London at age 46, shortly after publishing Nineteen Eighty-Four in 1949.
events.significance: Orwell's works, including Animal Farm and Nineteen Eighty-Four, remain enduring critiques of totalitarianism and have contributed terms such as 'Big Brother' and 'Orwellian' to the common language.

events.title: Concorde Commences Commercial Supersonic Service
events.description: British Airways and Air France simultaneously launched the first scheduled commercial supersonic passenger flights with Concorde, flying from London to Bahrain and from Paris to Rio de Janeiro.
events.significance: Concorde marked a milestone in aviation, cutting transatlantic travel time to about three and a half hours and remaining an icon of engineering until its retirement in 2003.

events.title: Launch of USS Nautilus
events.description: The USS Nautilus, the world's first operational nuclear-powered submarine, was launched at Groton, Connecticut, with First Lady Mamie Eisenhower breaking the traditional bottle of champagne.
events.significance: Nuclear propulsion allowed submarines to stay submerged for extended periods, transforming naval warfare and strategy during the Cold War.
